newsitem.title: USA: U.S. targets landlords who abuse federal programs.
newsitem.headline: U.S. targets landlords who abuse federal programs.

text.p: The U.S. government Monday lauched a crackdown on landlords who abuse federal housing programs, announcing that cases had already been filed in the New Orleans area, Dallas, Indianapolis and New York City.

Housing Secretary Andrew Cuomo and Attorney General Janet Reno said their departments would team up to file civil and criminal charges where warranted against bad landlords in the 50 communities with the largest concentration of federal-assisted housing.
"Our message is simple. If you are a landlord and you abuse your position, your lease is up," Cuomo said at a joint news conference with Reno.
"We are not in the business of subsidizing rich landlords so they can live in luxury while they let their tenants live in slums," he said.
Reno said U.S. attorneys across the country were ready to pursue cases against bad landlords referred by the Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) for possible prosecution.
"Landlords who receive federal funds must realize that if they don't play by the rules they will lose out in the end," Reno told reporters.
Penalties for abuse of federal housing programs include prison sentences, fines, civil fraud judgments, mortgage foreclosures, and bans on doing business with the federal government.
About 4.3 million low and moderate income people -- many of them elderly and disabled -- live in about 2.5 million HUD-assisted apartment units owned by private landlords.
